trigger: RBAC enforcement ON + a JIT-elevated built-in 'user' session (passes perm_fn via is_elevated, auth_routes.cpp:661) resets an account holding a user-principal RBAC Administrator grant whose built-in role is 'user'; also an OIDC admin-group session (session role=admin from resolve_role_from_groups, stored auth.users.role='user') is treated as a 'durable' admin
summary: Admin-reset 'durable administrator' rule forks is_rbac_administrator(): caller = Session::role==admin, target = auth.users.role column + AND role <> 'admin'; neither consults principal_roles, so under RBAC-on a time-boxed JIT elevation can re-key a standing RBAC Administrator (then log in as it); OIDC admin sessions counted 'durable' (arch-1). Docs advertise the guard (I6(a)). Fix: caller via is_rbac_administrator(*session, auth_db, rbac_store, RbacAdminSurface::kRest)==kAdmin + check_caller_authorized_under_current_regime (kUnavailable->503); target admin = built-in admin OR user-principal Administrator grant, read fail-closed; the grant half of the atomic guard must be a NEW RbacAdminAuthorityOwner method reusing kAuthenticatableAdminGrantsFrom (a principal_roles subquery inside AuthDB::set_password would violate A2/A1 routed-row CATASTROPHIC clause 1 — architect; authdb proposed an inline NOT EXISTS, overruled by that clause). Closure test: qe-2. Echoed/confirmed by architect (arch-1), authdb, consistency-auditor (con-4), compliance-officer (comp-5).
classification_rationale: Code contradicts the published contract ('administrator targets need a standing administrator'; 'the write itself refuses an administrator row') and auth-architecture.md:240/228-235. Not a policy floor: EXTEND-never-fork is a header comment; A2/A1 clause 3 concerns widening the predicate (architect adjudication).

trigger: A cookie+password holder (no second factor) performs repeated self-changes (A->A allowed) inside the 300 s step-up window; each re-mint passes mfa_verified=true -> create_local_session stamps mfa_verified_at=now() and a full kSessionDuration
summary: Self-change re-mint authors a fresh MFA proof instant and session lifetime with no new proof, so the step-up window and the session can be extended indefinitely without TOTP; the 'step-up above just required a fresh proof' comment and rest-api.md 'keeps the old one's MFA proof' are false. authdb adjudicated I1+E2 => CRITICAL (escapes the MFA re-auth bound; also carries a future-dated proof marked unusable). Fix: mint with mfa_verified=false, or carry the old DB-authored proof time via mfa_verified_ms_abs + remaining lifetime gated on steady_mfa_verified != {} (only correct shapes under the #3715 DB-clock contract — architect). Closure test: qe-3 / CH-1 / CH-4.
classification_rationale: Adjacent comment and docs contradict the code next to an authn branch; band HIGH per reporter, CRITICAL per authdb adjudication (E2) — gates either way.

trigger: Attacker /login with the OLD password before a change/reset, then /login/mfa or /login/mfa/enroll (MfaPending, 120 s TTL, survives invalidate_user_sessions) after it; worst case mfa_enforcement admin-only/required + unenrolled target lets the attacker re-park enrollment tokens and enroll their own TOTP after an incident-response reset
summary: #5274's hash recheck closes only verify-read->row-lock; post_mint_role_recheck checks role+active, never the hash, and MfaPending entries survive the session sweep, so a superseded credential can still mint a session (defeats admin reset as incident response). Fix: carry the verified hash_hex through MfaPending and create_local_session; post-mint recheck denies+revokes when get_user()->hash_hex differs; race-hook test (CH-5).
classification_rationale: The change advertises 'a change/reset ... revokes every session' and the #5274 deny; a pending login authenticated by the old credential still completes.

trigger: A v0.14.0 install whose admin password was 'rotated' via yuzu-server.cfg edit or Windows installer /ADMIN_PASS (never reached Postgres; only worked via cache-first read) upgrades to this build

Fix: state outright in the fragment (Breaking lead) + upgrading.md + server-admin.md that a cfg-/installer-rotated password reverts and must be re-rotated in product immediately if it was rotated for exposure; recommended code: boot-time WARN + counter (+ audit) when a cfg user's hash differs from auth.users or the user exists only in cfg. Independently raised by release-deploy (Gate 3) and compliance-officer comp-4 (Gate 6, shown rel-1 — echo; counted once more only because comp-4 adds I1/I3/I4/E0 facts).

Fix: on upgrade with /ADMIN_PASS refuse (exit 7) pointing to in-product reset, or warn in log + finish page; update both texts.
classification_rationale: Shipped installer guidance now contradicts runtime behaviour and conceals state (I4).

trigger: Admin reset while ApiTokenStore is degraded (pool lease timeout, query failure, or !open_)
summary: list_active_for_principal returns an empty vector on every failure (its own doc says indistinguishable from zero); the route emits api_tokens_active: 0 as authoritative and the dashboard shows a green success toast with no token warning (remediation hint dropped) — operator resetting a possibly-compromised account is told no tokens remain. Fix: checked accessor returning std::expected; emit null + api_tokens_unknown reason; toast warns whenever value is not a number; degraded-store test (CH-6).
classification_rationale: Response field documented as an authoritative count is wrong under degrade.

trigger: session_store_->invalidate_user fails (PG blip) during a change/reset; old cookie replayed on same or another replica
summary: invalidate_user_sessions wipes only the local cache when the durable delete fails; validate_session_durable misses cache, find() returns the undeleted row and re-admits the attacker's cookie on every replica; the toast says sessions were signed out and ignores sessions_db_persisted (arch-5's 'local wipe holds' assumption is false in store mode). Fix: treat a non-durable revoke on a credential change as a failure (non-2xx or explicit warning + retry), surface sessions_db_persisted in the UI, and/or fail closed; CH-1.
classification_rationale: 'revokes every session on every server' is advertised; a durable-revoke failure silently leaves them valid.

trigger: Admin reset (or self-change) of a LOCKED account, audit write fails, compensating rollback succeeds
summary: rollback_password_write -> set_password zeroes failed_login_count/last_failed_login_at/locked_until; the 500 says 'not applied' but the brute-force lock is gone with no auth.lockout.cleared row. VERIFIED on a disposable DB with the production SQL (locked row -> write -> rollback = failed_login_count=0, locked_until=NULL). The rollback comment calling this 'harmless' is contradicted. Fix: rollback must restore the prior lockout columns (snapshot them in PasswordWriteResult) or a rollback variant that does not touch them; CH-3. Echoed by compliance-officer comp-1/comp-2.
classification_rationale: Code comment claims harmlessness next to a security-control path; observed outcome contradicts it.

trigger: --auth-mode=sso-only; a break-glass cookie alive after disarm (8 h) or a local session minted before restart into sso-only; POST /api/v1/users/me/password with guessed current passwords
summary: password_change_verify_fn sets lockout_exempt for the break-glass account but no pre_verify_gate, so an UN-ARMED break-glass password is PBKDF2-evaluated with no lockout — breaks auth-architecture.md 'while un-armed, the password is never evaluated'; authentication.md:61 false; with sec-1 the re-mint keeps the session alive indefinitely. Fix: reuse /login's sso-only arm gate as pre_verify_gate (and drop the exemption when not armed); CH-4.
classification_rationale: Published sso-only/break-glass invariant does not hold on the new route.

trigger: --auth-mode=sso-only; an OIDC admin session (RBAC-off: role=admin from groups) or an OIDC principal with an RBAC Administrator grant (RBAC-on) calls POST /api/v1/users/{break_glass_user}/password
summary: Admin route has no break-glass/local-admin exclusion: a compromised IdP can invalidate the sealed escape-hatch password and revoke its sessions, defeating the 'survives IdP compromise' invariant the SCIM path protects (auth-architecture.md:1689). sec-2's is_rbac_administrator fix does not close the RBAC-on half. Bears directly on the accepted 'admin route accepts OIDC/SAML admin cookie sessions' decision. Fix: refuse local-credential mutation of the break-glass account (and arguably any local admin) from a non-local session.
classification_rationale: Contradicts the documented break-glass independence invariant.

trigger: In-product password rotation, then an empty auth.users (disaster rebuild, compose down -v, new Postgres) and restart; provision_first_admin re-seeds the cfg admin hash
summary: save_config is a no-op in AuthDB mode (auth.cpp:292), so an in-product rotation never updates yuzu-server.cfg; on an empty auth schema the OLD cfg password becomes admin again; no doc warns. Distinct from rel-1. Fix: document + boot WARN when seeding from a cfg older than the last in-product rotation, or require re-seeding confirmation; CH-8a.
classification_rationale: Security-relevant re-seed behaviour undocumented (I7) with an I1 outcome.

trigger: Process killed after the success audit commits and before invalidate_user_sessions
summary: Order is write -> audit ok -> revoke; a crash in the window leaves the attacker's durable sessions alive with an audit row claiming a reset and no session.revoke_all. Revoking before the write is always safe. Fix: revoke before the write (or make revoke idempotently retried at boot); CH-2 (provable by code read).
classification_rationale: Advertised 'change revokes sessions' does not hold across a crash window.

trigger: A local row with password_hash='' or salt_hex='' (schema NOT NULL DEFAULT ''), e.g. hand-seeded/direct-SQL, then a change/reset
summary: set_password refuses an empty expected hash with InvalidCredentials; write_password_cas maps it to kStoreUnavailable -> 503 'retry shortly' forever on a healthy store; an empty previous salt makes the rollback refuse, leaving the new password unaudited. I4 vs I8 is PENDING ADJUDICATION (reporter flagged): if the 503 text is harmful guidance concealing state -> HIGH; if merely degraded -> LOW. Recorded at the stronger value until adjudicated. Fix: map InvalidCredentials to a terminal named refusal (409/500 'stored credential malformed'), CH-10.
classification_rationale: Error text 'temporarily unavailable, retry' contradicts the actual permanent state.

summary: New test code cleans the temp cfg (unique_temp_path('yuzu_test_pwcfg_')) with a manual throwing fs::remove at lines 58/290/358 (Resource Ledger R17); leaks on early failure. Fix (cpp-safety): declare `yuzu::test::TempDir dir{"yuzu_test_pwcfg_"}; fs::create_directories(dir.path); const auto cfg = dir.path / "yuzu-server.cfg";` FIRST in each case and delete fresh_cfg_path() and all three removes. Confirmed by cpp-safety (csafe-1) and quality-engineer (qe-5).
classification_rationale: Policy floor, not derivation: derived LOW.

trigger: Intermittent get_user (or recheck QueryFailed) failure on the now DB-first login/self-change path while record_failed_login succeeds

summary: In the R5-inverted (~1694-1695) and R5b-inverted (~1737-1738) tests, `std::jthread admin_a;` is declared BEFORE `std::atomic<bool> fired{false};`. The hook stored in h.owner captures [&] and does fired.exchange(true); thread A's commit invokes it. On an exception unwind, `fired` is destroyed before ~jthread joins A, so A can touch `fired` after its lifetime ends (UB per [basic.life]: borrowed-data escape through a callback/thread). Move-assign into the dying admin_a refuted (A reads true and returns). ASan/UBSan cannot see it (trivially destructible stack object; scratch repro clean). Adjudicated by a focused cpp-safety pass as the policy floor; the earlier cpp-safety pass-4 statement 'each jthread declared after every local it captures' was false for hook-reached objects (orchestrator read the source). Fix: declare `fired` before `admin_a` at both sites. Other jthread sites checked: safe.
classification_rationale: Lifetime/ownership defect in new test code (cpp-safety blocking-contract class; contract has no test exclusion).
